verdicts.evidence:
Code read: replace_bell_group.py:136-142 compares the live file, calls acs.write_backup, compares the backup with `original`, then calls atomic_write. apply_claude_settings.py:208-209 opens `open(target, "rb")` and only then runs shutil.copyfileobj. All runs used a private copy and a synthetic HOME.
(1) Baseline `python3 -B evidence/artifacts/notification-types-20260929/replace_bell_group_controls.py <copy>`: "24 cases, 0 problems", exit=0.
(2) Scratch runner wrapping acs.shutil.copyfileobj so that, once the source is open, acs.atomic_write saves model='atomic-save-during-backup': "VF source inode differs from current live: True" / "backup written: settings.json.bak.20260930T064143Z" / "read-back equals the merged copy: True" / "VF tool exit: 0" / "VF FINAL LIVE MODEL original" / "VF BACKUP MODELS ['original']" / "VF ANY RECOVERY COPY HAS NEW SAVE False".
(3) Scratch harness whose at-backup mode was changed to that atomic interleaving: "WRONG a save that lands while the backup is taken is refused, the backup holds it and nothing is installed: exit 0, expected nonzero | ... the other writer's save was lost; the overlay's bell group was installed over the other writer's save; the backup does not hold the newer content" / "24 cases, 1 problems", exit=1.
(4) Deciding runs: an in-place (same-inode) save during the copy IS caught: "tool exit: 1 | FINAL LIVE MODEL newer-save | BACKUP MODELS ['newer-save']". An atomic save in the gap the docstring already admits (after the backup comparison, before atomic_write): "tool exit: 0 | VF FINAL LIVE MODEL original | VF BACKUP MODELS ['original'] | VF ANY COPY HAS NEWER SAVE False". So the parenthetical at lines 13-14, "(the backup then holds it)", is false even for that admitted gap.
Why medium, not high: the new window (source open to copy) lasts microseconds, the same order as the compare-to-replace race the docstring already concedes. The loss needs a rename-based save that coincides with it, which is wrong edge behavior. The docs overstate the protection: README row 14 and docs/decisions/2026-09-28-terminal-experience.md:365 say "installs only over the bytes it read", and the docstring says the backup holds a late save.
verdicts.fix_assessment: Sufficient for the reported window, and safe because it only adds refusals: comparing the live file with `original` again after the backup catches a rename made after the source was opened. It cannot close the final comparison-to-os.replace gap; that would need cooperative locking or a RENAME_EXCHANGE-style swap. So the wording correction is required, and it must also reach README row 14 and decision record line 365, not only docstring line 14. The proposed control must inject a rename after the source is opened. The existing harness does an in-place write before write_backup, which cannot fail this way. A matching mutant in replace_bell_group_mutants.py would prove the new comparison is load-bearing.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In replace_bell_group.py, re-read live_path after write_backup and the backup comparison, refuse unless it still equals `original`, then call atomic_write. Reword docstring lines 13-14, README row 14 and decision line 365 to say a save that lands between that last comparison and the replace is overwritten and kept in no copy. Add an atomic-after-open mode to concurrent_writer_harness.py with one control case.
verdicts.adjacent: The control that claims this protection cannot exercise it. replace_bell_group_controls.py:199-200 ("a save that lands while the backup is taken is refused, the backup holds it") uses concurrent_writer_harness.py:37-43, which runs other_writer() (an in-place Path.write_text, lines 17-20) before the real write_backup opens the file. The save therefore never happens during the copy and is never a rename. Verified: the unmodified controls pass 24/24, and the same case becomes WRONG only when the injection is changed to an atomic save after the source is opened (run 3).

verdicts.evidence:
Code read: alert_probe.py:293-299 opens the pty, runs Popen (start_new_session=True), then os.close(slave). The try/finally that runs os.killpg starts at line 333. In push_notification_probe.py, Popen is at 294-296, os.close(slave) at 297 and the try at 335. with_private_dir's docstring (alert_probe.py:251-252) says the finally that stops the child process group runs for SIGTERM/SIGHUP.
Scratch runner used sys.settrace to signal itself at the os.close(slave) line. A stand-in `claude` (`exec sleep <unique>`) was first on PATH, with a synthetic HOME and TMPDIR. Results:
- alert_probe.py SIGTERM: "VF sending SIGTERM at alert_probe.py:299" / "raw payload directory removed: True" / exit=143 / "private directory exists False | child still running True"
- alert_probe.py SIGHUP: exit=129, same result
- push_notification_probe.py SIGTERM at :297: exit=143; SIGHUP: exit=129; both "private directory exists False | child still running True"
Window size, from an instrumented copy with the stand-in, 3 runs: "Popen call 0.421/0.371/0.346 ms | Popen return to first line inside try 0.145/0.135/0.188 ms". That is about 0.5 ms per run, in runs that last 25-260 s.
Why low, not medium: the private directory is still removed, and the only consequence is an orphaned client that has not yet been sent a prompt. It needs a sub-millisecond coincidence, which puts it at hygiene level; the docstring overstates coverage only for this window. What the real client does after the pty master closes could not be checked here. The reproduction uses the probe's own stand-in model, which its --selftest signal_case also relies on.
verdicts.fix_assessment: The direction is right: guard before creating the pty and the client, track which resources exist, and add a boundary signal case. One caution about "protect process creation from interruption". If it is done with signal.pthread_sigmask around Popen, the client inherits the blocked mask across exec. Verified: with SIGTERM blocked in the parent, a Popen child showed SigBlk 0000000000004000 (signal 15 blocked). The probe's later os.killpg(SIGTERM) would then be ignored until the SIGKILL. A deferring handler avoids this: it records a signal that arrives during the spawn and raises once `proc` is assigned. The proposal covers only SIGTERM/SIGHUP, but SIGINT at the same boundary also orphans the client (see adjacent).
verdicts.smallest_repair: In measure() of both probes, set master and proc to None and enter the try/finally before pty.openpty(), skipping killpg/wait/close for resources that are still None. Have the handler defer SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT that arrive during Popen until proc is assigned. Add a --selftest case that signals at the spawn boundary and asserts the stand-in is gone.
verdicts.adjacent: SIGINT (Ctrl-C) at the same boundary leaves the client running in both probes. This path predates the change and is outside the reviewer's SIGTERM/SIGHUP fix. alert_probe.py, signal at line 299: "raw payload directory removed: True", "KeyboardInterrupt", shell exit 130, and one stand-in still running afterwards (it was then killed). push_notification_probe.py, signal at line 297: returncode -2, "private directory exists False | child still running True".

verdicts.evidence:
Code read: alert_probe.py:262-263 restores the previous handlers, then line 264 runs shutil.rmtree(private, ignore_errors=True). The brief's "lines 263-264" covers the restore plus rmtree. In push_notification_probe.py the handlers are restored at 255-256 and rmtree runs at 257.
Scratch runner patched shutil.rmtree to send SIGTERM to itself on entry for the alert-probe-* directory. A stand-in client wrote a synthetic PreToolUse payload line into events.log 8 s after start, so measure() returned normally. Results:
- alert_probe.py ask: "VF SIGTERM at rmtree entry" / exit=143 / "private directories left 1 | payload retained True"
- push_notification_probe.py ask: "VF SIGTERM at rmtree entry" / exit=143 / "private directories left 1 | payload retained True"
Window size: rmtree of a private directory holding one 2 KB file took "median 57 us, max 96 us" over 200 runs, and the window opens only after the handlers are restored.
Why low, not medium: the left-behind directory is mkdtemp's 0700 directory in the user's own TMPDIR, and the window is about 0.1 ms after a run of at least 25 s. That is a hygiene-level consequence in a coincidence window.
verdicts.fix_assessment: The reviewer is right that moving the restore below rmtree is not enough: a raising handler would then interrupt rmtree, and ignore_errors does not catch SystemExit. Blocking SIGTERM/SIGHUP with signal.pthread_sigmask during cleanup, restoring the handlers and then unblocking is safe here, because no child is spawned during cleanup and so nothing inherits the mask. Any pending signal is delivered after the directory is gone. As proposed it covers only with_private_dir. SIGINT should be blocked too, and measure()'s finally has the same exposure with a much larger window (see adjacent).
verdicts.smallest_repair: In both probes, block SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT with signal.pthread_sigmask at the start of cleanup (both with_private_dir's finally and measure()'s finally). Run the cleanup, restore the previous handlers, then unblock. Add a --selftest case that signals at rmtree entry and asserts the directory is gone.
verdicts.adjacent:
A repeated signal interrupts measure()'s process-group cleanup before os.killpg. The scratch driver started each probe with the stand-in, sent a signal 1.5 s after the private directory appeared, and a second one 0.3 s later.
- alert_probe.py: "SIGTERM x1: exit 143 | private directory left False", stand-in alive False; "SIGTERM x2: exit 143 | private directory left False", stand-in alive True; "SIGINT x2: exit -2 | private directory left False", stand-in alive True.
- push_notification_probe.py: the same pattern (x1 False, SIGTERM x2 True, SIGINT x2 True).
The exposure is the ~1.8 s of sleeps in measure()'s finally (alert_probe.py:375-384, push_notification_probe.py:385-394), and a double Ctrl-C reaches it. This leaves the client running and is more consequential than F-sol-R1-3 itself: medium, as wrong edge behavior.

verdicts.fix_assessment: The reviewer's direction and both proposed controls are right and would catch the gap. A third control is also needed, for a changed one-line attribute: today no check touches attributes at all, since the empty-prefix mutant passes. Beware the obvious implementation. A lazy `#\[.*?\]\n` under re.S is unsafe because the leftmost re.search starts at the first `#[` in the file. The NotificationMethod capture grows to 341 vs 184 characters on SYNTHETIC and 19,592 vs 184 on the upstream file, and it flips the real 0.157.1->0.159.0 comparison to False. A bracket-bounded alternative `[ \t]*#\[[^\[\]]*\][ \t]*\n` avoids this: it gives the same output as today on SYNTHETIC and on both upstream tags (True), and returns False for the reviewer's case and for the wrapped-derive variant. The reviewer's "return unknown when extraction cannot account for them" can be done by returning None when the line directly above the captured block is not blank, a closing `}` or the start of the file.

verdicts.evidence: Checked in checkout 9e55a103; git status was still clean afterwards. At login_shell_check_controls.py:56 the probe reads `if p=$(type -P "$c") && [ -n "$p" ]; then echo "FOUND:$c"`. The profiles start the client with `bash -lc "exec claude"` (examples/claude-native/windows-terminal.fragment.example.json:27). I ran a python3 -B harness in a scratch copy (<scratch>, since deleted) that imports login_shell_check, with a temporary HOME. Home S has a .bash_profile containing `hash -p "$HOME/missing/<n>" <n>` for claude, codex, nativestack and rtk. Result: `S stale-hash home: login_shell_check -> {"pass": true, "missing_in_login_shell": [], "empty_files_shadowing_profile": [], "probe_completed": true, "exit": 0}`. The same home through env -i /bin/bash -lc gave: `type -P claude -> <home>/missing/claude` / `test -e exit 1` / `test -x exit 1` / `/bin/bash: line 1: <home>/missing/claude: No such file or directory` / `exec claude: exit 127`. Control home C (claude absent) gave `{"pass": false, "missing_in_login_shell": ["claude"], ...}`. In plain bash 5.2.21, `hash -p /nonexistent/dir/claude claude; type -P claude` printed `/nonexistent/dir/claude` / `type -P exit 0`. The shipped controls gave `exit 0 <- python3 -B login_shell_check_controls.py` with `all_cases_as_expected True cases 9`; none of the nine homes has a hashed or non-executable path. The Bash Reference Manual (fetched 2026-09-30) says: 'If a name is present in the table of hashed commands, options -p and -P print the hashed value, which is not necessarily the file that appears first in $PATH.' On checkhash (off by default, so exec runs the stale hashed path) it says: 'If this is set, Bash checks that a command found in the hash table exists before trying to execute it.' Severity is medium (wrong edge behaviour). The reviewer's trigger needs a startup file that runs hash -p, which is contrived, but the adjacent trigger below is not.
verdicts.fix_assessment: The fix is sufficient and safe. Requiring the printed path to pass [ -f "$p" ] && [ -x "$p" ] rejects the stale hash (exec gives 127) and bash's fallback to a non-executable file (exec gives 126). It also matches what exec does: with checkhash off, exec uses the hashed path, so the check and the profile fail together. A symlink to an executable still passes, because -f and -x follow links. The check would only become stricter than exec if a startup file set checkhash, and that fails closed. The proposed control is incomplete: it covers only the stale hash. A home with a non-executable file named claude on PATH must also be a required-fail case, because that trigger needs no contrived startup file. The docstring describes this function as a copy of the practice repository's doctor, which needs the same change. That repository is not in the checkout, so I could not check it.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In login_shell_check_controls.py:56 (and in the practice doctor), print FOUND only when the type -P output is a regular executable file ([ -f "$p" ] && [ -x "$p" ]). Add two homes that must fail: one with stale hash -p entries and one with a mode-0644 claude on PATH. Reword the 'type -P finds files only' sentences to say the printed path must also pass test -x.
verdicts.adjacent: Verified: the same predicate, with a different trigger. When no executable matches, bash's type -P falls back to a non-executable regular file on PATH. Home N (bin/claude mode 0644, the other three names executable) gave `N non-executable claude: mode 0o644 login_shell_check -> {"pass": true, "missing_in_login_shell": [], "empty_files_shadowing_profile": [], "probe_completed": true, "exit": 0}`. The same home gave `type -P claude -> <home>/bin/claude` / `test -e exit 0` / `test -x exit 1` / `/bin/bash: line 1: exec: <home>/bin/claude: cannot execute: Permission denied` / `exec claude: exit 126`. The same wording appears in text added in f2a169d0: docstring lines 12-13 and evidence/artifacts/login-shell-contract-20260929/README.md:16 ('`type -P` finds files only'). It also appears in the manual probes at adoption/platforms/linux-wsl2.md:193 ('must print both paths (`type -P` finds files only; ...)') and recipes/claude-native-profile.md:108; both accept any printed path as success.

verdicts.evidence: tmux_sync_probe.py:4 says 'Reads and writes only inside its own temporary directory; kills only its own server.' Lines 12-13 build `-L sync{os.getpid()}`, and lines 22 (the pty child) and 42 (the finally block) also use -L. I ran it in the scratch copy under env -u TMUX, with HOME, TMPDIR and TMUX_TMPDIR each set to a scratch directory. Output: `tmux: tmux 3.4` / `... with terminal-features xterm*:sync: (3, 3)` / `the same without it (negative control): (0, 0)` / `synchronized output is emitted only when declared: True` / `exit 0 <- python3 -B tmux_sync_probe.py`. Afterwards `entries in TMPDIR: 0` (the ts* directories are gone), but `tmux-1000/sync3706597  type=s` remains. `tmux -S <that socket> list-sessions` printed `no server running on <TMUX_TMPDIR>/tmux-1000/sync3706597`. The run stayed isolated: `real /tmp/tmux-1000 sync* entries before: 6` / `after: 6`. The tmux 3.4 tmux.1 (fetched) says that with -L 'the sockets are all created in a directory tmux-UID under the directory given by TMUX_TMPDIR or in /tmp'. Supporting observation, though origin is not proven: the shared /tmp/tmux-1000 already holds 6 sync<pid> and 12 probe<pid> socket entries dated 2026-09-29 15:56 to 2026-09-30 02:00, and `pgrep -fc 'tmux -L (sync|probe)[0-9]'` returns 0. The names match the two probes' naming patterns. Severity is low: a dead socket in the user's own 0700 directory, which tmux unlinks before its next bind, so there is no data loss, only an inaccurate claim and clutter.
verdicts.fix_assessment: The fix is sufficient and safe. -S <work>/<name> puts the socket in the private directory, and the existing finally order (kill-server, then rmtree) removes it. Three call sites must change, not one: base (line 13), the pty child's own argv (line 22) and the finally kill-server (line 42). mkdtemp must also move before base is built. An equally small alternative is to set TMUX_TMPDIR=<work> for every tmux invocation, including the child's execv environment. A long TMPDIR could push the socket path past the sun_path limit; tmux then fails and the probe exits nonzero, which is safe. Only unlinking the -L socket afterwards would remove the leftover but still leave the docstring's claim false.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In tmux_sync_probe.py, create the work directory first and pass -S <work>/s (or TMUX_TMPDIR=<work>) to every tmux call, including the attach child and the finally kill-server, so rmtree removes the socket. Apply the same change to notification-types-20260929/tmux_bell_probe.py.

verdicts.evidence: login_path_digest.py:43-45 checks lines[-1] == 'DONE' and lines[0].startswith('PATH='), then hashes lines[0][5:]. `python3 -B -c 'import hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(b"logged-before-final-path").hexdigest()[:16])'` -> 2872b9f4cd092719. So the reviewer's digest is the hash of the log line itself. Reproduction in a scratch copy (since removed) used two temporary HOMEs. Each .bash_profile runs `echo "PATH=logged-before-final-path"` and then `PATH="/synthetic/first:$PATH"` (the second home uses /synthetic/second). `env HOME=<tmp> python3 -B evidence/artifacts/login-shell-contract-20260929/login_path_digest.py` printed '{"login_path_entries": 1, "login_path_sha256_prefix": "2872b9f4cd092719", "distro_default_path_entries": 9}' with exit=0 for both. An independent capture used the script's own env -i (HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, distro default PATH) and /bin/bash -lc 'printf "@@S@@%s@@E@@" "$PATH"'. It gave 'f2a | bash exit 0 | final PATH entries 10 | sha256 prefix 2755fd727acd8653' and 'f2b | bash exit 0 | final PATH entries 10 | sha256 prefix 36fd9d2c29da5499'. A newline component (PATH=$'/syn\nthetic:'"$PATH") gave CLI '{"login_path_entries": 1, "login_path_sha256_prefix": "19374fa059add4e5", ...}' exit=0. sha256(b'/syn')[:16] is 19374fa059add4e5, so the PATH was truncated at the newline; the real final PATH has 10 entries (7aa7316f4d611857). `--selftest` -> '{"selftest_cases": 4, "problems": []}' exit=0; it has no startup-output case.
verdicts.fix_assessment: Sufficient and safe, provided the hashed payload stays byte-identical to the old input (the PATH with no trailing newline). That keeps the docstring's promise that old and new digests compare. Use a per-run nonce (or NUL framing) so startup output cannot forge the frame, and take the last record. 'Binary-safe' is justified. A .bash_profile that prints byte \377 before setting PATH crashes the unmodified CLI with 'UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte' (exit 1, no JSON line). The cause is that stdout is decoded as text, and the crash contradicts the documented measurement_error contract. Tests that assert exact entry counts and digests are the right control.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In measure() (login_path_digest.py:36-45), print the PATH inside a per-run nonce frame as the last output and capture it as bytes. Extract the last framed payload, hash it whole, and report measurement_error when the frame is missing or malformed. Add selftest homes with a 'PATH=...' log line, a plain 'echo hello' line and a newline-containing component, each asserting exact entries and digest.
verdicts.adjacent: Same positional line parsing, failing the other way. A healthy home whose .bash_profile is `echo hello` then `PATH="/synthetic/first:$PATH"` gets '{"measurement_error": "the login shell ended before the PATH probe completed", "bash_exit": 0}' with exit=1. Yet bash exited 0, and the sentinel capture measured its final PATH (10 entries, 2755fd727acd8653). The docstring treats only a nonzero exit, a missing DONE or a missing PATH line as an error, and here none of those happened.

verdicts.evidence: alert_probe.py:255-258 installs leave() (raise SystemExit(128 + signum)) for SIGTERM and SIGHUP. The handlers are restored only in with_private_dir's finally (262-264). That runs after measure()'s finally (374-391), whose ESC and Ctrl-C writes each sleep 0.5 s before os.killpg (382-384), and nothing there catches SystemExit. push_notification_probe.py:248-257 and 384-396 have the same structure. Scratch harness (copy since removed): a temporary HOME with code/native-agent-stack, a stand-in `claude` first on PATH (`echo $$ > pidfile; exec /bin/sleep 300`), and a private TMPDIR. Signals were sent 1.0 s after the pidfile appeared. Results: 'alert_probe ask | 1 x SIGTERM | probe exit 143 | stand-in alive before signal True | stand-in after probe exit: gone'. 'alert_probe ask | 2 x SIGTERM 100 ms apart | probe exit 143 | stand-in alive before signal True | stand-in after probe exit: ALIVE (S (sleeping); cmdline '/bin/sleep 300') | private dirs left 0 | probe last line ['raw payload directory removed: True']'. push --no-user-settings: 1 x SIGTERM 'gone'; 2 x SIGTERM 'ALIVE (S (sleeping); cmdline '/bin/sleep 300')'. Two SIGHUPs give exit 129 and ALIVE in both probes, while one SIGHUP leaves it 'gone'. verification.json verdicts[18].fix_assessment reads: 'A repeated signal during cleanup should be ignored.' Not tested: whether the real client exits by itself once its pty master closes, which needs a sign-in. What is shown is that the probes' documented cleanup contract breaks.
verdicts.fix_assessment: Right direction, but insufficient as worded. (1) 'Once shutdown begins' has to mean entry to measure()'s finally, not just the first signal: one signal during the normal-exit cleanup already leaks the client (see adjacent). (2) SIGINT must be covered as well. Two SIGINTs 100 ms apart (a double Ctrl-C) give 'probe exit -2 | ... stand-in after probe exit: ALIVE (S (sleeping); cmdline '/bin/sleep 300')' in both probes, while one SIGINT leaves it 'gone'. KeyboardInterrupt aborts the same finally. Otherwise the fix is safe. Restoring the handlers after rmtree is correct, and the proposed two-signal test with a live-before and gone-after PID check is good. Add a double-SIGINT case and a signal-during-normal-cleanup case.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In both probes, set SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGINT to SIG_IGN on entry to measure()'s finally (and in leave() before it raises). Restore the saved handlers in with_private_dir's finally after rmtree. Add subprocess tests for two SIGTERMs, two SIGINTs and one SIGTERM during normal cleanup, each checking the stand-in PID is alive before and gone after.
verdicts.adjacent: Same root cause (the cleanup finally can be interrupted), verified in both probes. A stand-in that prints trust-dialog text makes the probe abort by itself at about 6 s. One SIGTERM sent 6.6 s after the stand-in started, while the normal-exit cleanup was sleeping, gave 'probe exit 143 | no summary line (cleanup was interrupted) | stand-in alive after exit: True'. The no-signal control gave 'probe exit 2 | kind=ask control=False state=aborted dialog_opened=False probe_process_group=gone | stand-in alive after exit: False', and the push probe behaved the same. A single signal is enough, so masking only after a first signal would not close this.

verdicts.evidence: alert_probe.py:124-126 sets started = bool(list(tmp.glob('alert-probe-*'))), which checks only the probe's private directory. Line 142 is ok = started and not left_dirs and not alive. alive scans /proc for the stand-in's unique sleep argument, so a stand-in that never ran counts as not alive. push_notification_probe.py:126-128 and 144 have the same code. Each mutant copy (mutation site count checked as 1) ran --selftest with a temporary HOME holding code/native-agent-stack. 'alert_probe.py | unmodified | --selftest exit 0 | FAIL lines 0 | ['PASS SIGTERM end to end: probe started True, private directory left False, stand-in client still alive False']'. 'alert_probe.py | client never starts (/bin/true launched instead of claude) | --selftest exit 0 | FAIL lines 0 | ['PASS SIGTERM end to end: probe started True, private directory left False, stand-in client still alive False']'. push_notification_probe.py gave the same for both. A calibration mutant replaced both os.killpg lines with pass: 'calibration: the process group is never killed | --selftest exit 1 | FAIL lines 1 | ['FAIL SIGTERM end to end: probe started True, private directory left False, stand-in client still alive True']' in both probes. So the control can fail; the gap is that it passes vacuously because it never asserts the client started. That makes its PASS line an unsupported claim, hence medium. A broken launcher would also show up in a real run as exit 2 ('the dialog never opened').
verdicts.fix_assessment: Sufficient and safe. Keep the unique-cmdline check alongside the PID check to guard against PID reuse. The PASS line text changes, so evidence/artifacts/terminal-lane-cross-family-review-20260930/recorded/alert_probe_selftest.txt and recorded/push_notification_probe_selftest.txt must be re-recorded. Put the never-started mutant into a mutant runner so the control is required to reject it.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In signal_case of both probes, have the stand-in write its PID to a file in the sigcase directory (exec keeps the PID). Fail when the file never appears or that process is not alive before the SIGTERM, and require the PID to be gone afterwards.
